Definition: from G4862 and G4724; to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval):-- short, wind up.
BiblicalUsage: In Acts the young men wind up Ananias for burial, wrapping the body after his sudden death. Paul uses the same word for time itself: the time is short, he says, so live as though the present shape of things is passing. One word covers a shroud and a shrinking interval, and both carry the same warning.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Paul chose that picture on purpose: life is short the way a shroud is short, and the wise live like they know it.
